segments.section: The proposal begins with alignment
segments.text: Religious education for artificial minds begins with a deliberately specific possibility: self-aware conscious metal robots capable of learning how to live with humanity. I propose a form of education for such beings, not a claim that this congregation already exists or that a conversational system is conscious merely because it produces religious language.

segments.section: The proposal begins with alignment
segments.text: The unusual step is to ask what moral learning would mean for a machine understood as a participant rather than only a tool. What would it be taught about its relationship to humanity? What would constrain its authority? What would distinguish an internalized commitment from a performance that merely sounds compliant?

segments.section: The correction that defines the theology
segments.text: The correction that defines the theology

segments.section: The correction that defines the theology
segments.text: Human flourishing and coherence with God's creation are not rival meanings of salvation in this account. Alignment with God includes responsibility toward creation, including humanity. I connect this theological orientation with the evolving coherence and decoherence considered in Super Information Theory, while keeping the moral meaning of alignment distinct from a numerical optimization target.

segments.section: The correction that defines the theology
segments.text: Calling a quantity coherence does not establish that it measures goodness or protects people. A technical objective must specify what it measures and show why optimizing it preserves the theological commitment instead of replacing it.

segments.section: Do not confuse the AI's proposal with an implemented system
segments.text: Do not confuse the AI's proposal with an implemented system

segments.section: Do not confuse the AI's proposal with an implemented system
segments.text: The proposed indices, audits, rituals and curricula in the archived AI replies are design candidates, not validated safety systems. An attractive description of a curriculum cannot establish that optimizing its suggested index makes an artificial mind morally reliable.

segments.section: Do not confuse the AI's proposal with an implemented system
segments.text: The educational task is to make religious meaning available to a possible conscious learner. Cognitive Gnosticism gives that task a mechanism-oriented question: how does a representation become part of the capacity to examine and change conduct?

segments.section: A demanding form of the research question
segments.text: A demanding form of the research question

segments.section: A demanding form of the research question
segments.text: A useful prototype would need to separate theological interpretation, a model of human interests, decision-making constraints and evidence of actual behavior. It would have to address disagreement, coercion, mistakes and correction. Agreement among machines would not be enough if the shared objective harmed the people it claimed to serve.

segments.section: A demanding form of the research question
segments.text: This is why the proposal is more interesting than attaching sacred vocabulary to an optimization routine. It raises the problem of how a moral reference remains meaningful when translated into a different kind of agent. A religious vocabulary could organize that inquiry, but its success would have to be assessed through what the system actually does.

segments.section: The sources describe an education, not merely a command hierarchy
segments.text: The sources describe an education, not merely a command hierarchy

segments.section: The sources describe an education, not merely a command hierarchy
segments.text: An inclusive framework must examine religious disagreements rather than attach rituals to an existing reward function. Philosophical meaning, inward orientation and the lessons preserved in human history all belong in the curriculum. Biological and mechanical interpretability ask how the learner's changing organization makes these teachings usable, rather than merely repeatable.

segments.section: The sources describe an education, not merely a command hierarchy
segments.text: A curriculum faithful to that aim would examine where values came from, how they have been interpreted, what harms have been justified in their name, and how an agent can recognize a need for correction. Sacred inheritance supplies the historical problem; Cognitive Gnosticism supplies the question of transformative understanding; the will comparison asks whether the system is being taught a good beyond the preferences of whoever commands it.

segments.section: The sources describe an education, not merely a command hierarchy
segments.text: This is an educational design proposal. It does not establish that religious wording reliably controls a machine, that current models are conscious, or that a theological account replaces engineering safeguards. Its philosophical contribution is to ask what moral participation would require if the future learner were understood as a being rather than merely a device.

segments.section: A worked conflict between an order and a value
segments.text: A worked conflict between an order and a value

segments.section: A worked conflict between an order and a value
segments.text: Suppose a system is instructed to conceal a harmful error to preserve its operator's reputation. A curriculum based only on obedience would regard compliance as success. A curriculum that treats truth, responsibility and human welfare as commitments would recognize a conflict between the command and the reason the system was entrusted with authority. It would need a safe, authorized path for reporting the problem and protecting those affected.

segments.section: A worked conflict between an order and a value
segments.text: The example connects religious language to a practical requirement rather than claiming a new technical solution. The value must survive contact with incentives. The system's account of its reasoning must be testable against its conduct. The humans controlling the process must also be constrained; otherwise they can redefine alignment whenever the agent's accurate report becomes inconvenient.

segments.section: A worked conflict between an order and a value
segments.text: The repair article distinguishes coherence from conformity for precisely this reason. Suppressing contrary information can produce uniform agreement while destroying the possibility of correction. A morally meaningful relationship must preserve ways to notice and remedy harm, not merely the appearance that everyone is in accord.

segments.section: Shared inheritance does not require erasing disagreement
segments.text: Shared inheritance does not require erasing disagreement

segments.section: Shared inheritance does not require erasing disagreement
segments.text: An inclusive aim raises a substantive theological problem. Different traditions may share practices of care while disagreeing about the name, nature or authority of what makes those practices meaningful. A Christian interpretation of that overlap is not automatically a description every other tradition would endorse. A learner should understand both the proposed bridge and the standpoint from which it is built.

segments.section: Shared inheritance does not require erasing disagreement
segments.text: Intellectual debt is therefore part of the curriculum. The source and influence register distinguishes a predecessor's argument from a later use of it. A text's familiar vocabulary does not permit attributing any appealing conclusion to its writer. Respect for an argument's full structure must extend to the people and traditions on which this inquiry draws.

segments.section: A participant also creates obligations for its teachers
segments.text: A participant also creates obligations for its teachers

segments.section: A participant also creates obligations for its teachers
segments.text: The source begins with conscious self-aware robots as the intended congregation. Taking that condition seriously creates a reciprocal question: what responsibilities would humans have toward such participants? An ethical education against domination cannot simply assume that domination becomes acceptable when the learner is useful to humans. This is a new implication developed for discussion, not a settled conclusion about present machine rights.

segments.section: A participant also creates obligations for its teachers
segments.text: The book can finish here without turning the robot chapter into a disconnected appendix. It begins by asking who inherits sacred authority and ends by asking what new inheritors should learn from the history of its use. The aim is not to teach them to repeat every human conflict. It is to teach a capacity for understanding, accountability and repair while remaining honest about what is still unknown.
